shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Farkleberry / sparkleberry: woody shrub or small tree with ALTERNATE, small, glossy, leathery obovate/oblong leaves and pale undersides; clusters of small WHITE URN/BELL flowers followed by glossy BLACK small berries. Poricidal anthers confirm Ericaceae; compare carefully with Arbutus madrone.
shared_genus_recognition.identity_warning: Source-pool reference only, exact-species full scientific review and range status handled separately

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Shrub or small tree often with multiple trunks in xeric sandy or rocky eastern Texas woodlands
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Texas madrone can also be shrub/tree: do not identify from habit.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Gray/brown flaky or subtly peeling bark, NOT the dramatic smooth cream/salmon/exfoliating colors of Texas madrone
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Arbutus xalapensis mature bark smooth peeling and multi-colored; juvenile madrone ambiguity possible.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Simple alternate leathery obovate/oblong ~2.2–4 cm long, glossy above, somewhat glaucous beneath
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Arbutus often larger evergreen leaves; inspect multiple leaves and bark.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Small white urn/bell-shaped fused corolla ~3–5 mm; clustered stalked flowers
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Ericaceae flower plan shared with Arbutus; flower alone doesn't split.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Small black shiny berries ~7–9 mm at maturity
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Arbutus fruit orange/red at maturity; color variable in immature fruit.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Anthers releasing pollen via apical pores/tubules in dissected flower
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Compare with other Ericaceae (Arbutus, Rhododendron), not woody lookalikes outside Ericaceae.

look_here_first_sequence: Recognize plant architecture and leaf arrangement before flower color.
Compare leaf shape, insertion and microstructures on several mature samples.
Inspect floral anatomy under magnification and track into mature fruit.
Cross-check the strongest lookalike with matched scale; avoid uncertain species IDs.
Respect the source-name/canonical manifest boundary and keep nonlocal native labels unchanged.
scientific_cautions: V. arboreum is not currently installed despite Sheet source listing. Do not mark as native to Hays County or project target zone from state-wide FNA occurrence.
Evergreen/semi-evergreen degree varies seasonally and regionally; do not use leaf persistence as an absolute distinction.
Black mature berries, not blueberry cultivated form alone; fruit coloration and pubescence require a mature specimen.
